text: One day, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and the scribes came up with the elders
and said to him, "Tell us by what authority you do these things. Who gave you this authority?"
He answered them, "I will ask you a question too. Tell me:
Was John's baptism from heaven, or from men?"
They discussed it among themselves: "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Why didn't you believe him?'
But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they answered that they did not know where it came from.
And Jesus said to them, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
Then he began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard, leased it to tenant farmers, and went abroad for a long time.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
He sent another servant, and that one too they beat and humiliated and sent away empty-handed.
He sent yet a third, and this one they wounded and threw out.
Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.'
But when the tenants saw him, they reasoned with one another and said, 'This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours.'
So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others." When they heard this, they said, "May it never be!"
But he looked straight at them and said, "Then what does this mean that is written: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and anyone on whom it falls will be crushed."
The scribes and the chief priests wanted to lay hands on him that very hour, but they were afraid of the people, for they knew he had told this parable against them.
So they watched him closely and sent spies who pretended to be righteous, hoping to catch him in something he said, so they could hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.

versions.text: So they watched him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere, hoping to catch him in something he said, so they could hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
versions.explanation: δικαίους means "righteous/upright," a moral-religious claim, not merely "sincere." The stronger term better conveys the hypocrisy the text describes and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: They questioned him: "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and that you show no partiality, but teach the way of God truthfully.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
But he saw through their cunning and said to them,
"Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?" "Caesar's," they answered.
He said to them, "Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God."
They were unable to trap him in what he said in front of the people, and amazed at his answer, they fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came to him and asked,

versions.text: Some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and asked,
versions.explanation: ἀντιλέγοντες carries the sense of contradicting or denying, which is stronger and more precise than the neutral "say."

text: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies leaving a wife but no children, the man must take the widow and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless.
Then the second
and the third took her, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
Finally the woman died as well.
In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife."
Jesus said to them, "The people of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those considered worthy of taking part in that age and in the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
They can no longer die, for they are like the angels; and they are children of God, since they are children of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, where he calls the Lord 'the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to him all are alive."
Some of the scribes responded, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
For they no longer dared to ask him anything.

versions.text: And no one dared to ask him any more questions.
versions.explanation: The Greek verb is third person plural ("they no longer dared"), referring to the questioners just mentioned, and the explanatory γάρ ("for") links this verse to the preceding one. "No one" broadens the subject unnecessarily and drops the connective.

text: Then he said to them, "How can they say that the Christ is David's son?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
David calls him Lord; how then can he be his son?"
While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
"Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
They devour widows' houses and for show make lengthy prayers. These will receive a greater condemnation."
